issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car, the temperature gauge climbs or the engine overheats, and the oil may look milky or brown. In bad cases the engine knocks, blows white exhaust smoke or quits.
issues.why: On both V6 engines the water pump sits inside the engine, behind the timing chain, and is driven by it. When its seal wears out, coolant can leak straight into the oil instead of dripping outside, which thins the oil and can destroy the bearings. Owners report failures most often around 90,000-110,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant reservoir regularly. If the level drops for no visible reason or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have a cooling system pressure test and oil check done. Catching it early can save the engine; many owners replace the pump with the timing chain while the engine is apart.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit (PTU) overheats, leaks or fails
issues.sym: A propane-like or burning-oil smell at idle or low speed, gear oil dripping onto the exhaust near the front of the transmission, or a whine, clunk or grinding noise from the front of the car on AWD models.
issues.why: The PTU is a small gearbox that sends power to the rear wheels. It sits right next to the hot exhaust and holds very little fluid, so the fluid can cook and break down, which wears the idler gear bearing and seals. Ford issued service bulletins for odor, venting and noise and released a bearing rebuild kit.
issues.next: If you smell a gas-like or burnt odor, have the PTU checked for leaks and burnt fluid. Changing the PTU fluid now and then helps. A leaking seal is a modest repair; a PTU that is grinding usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Power steering assist can suddenly shut off (recall)
issues.sym: The steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at low speeds or when parking, and a steering warning may appear.
issues.why: A sensor fault in the electric power steering motor can make the system shut off its assist. The recall covers 2011-2012 MKTs with the EcoBoost engine and all 2013 MKTs.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer will update the software or replace the steering gear free.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can overheat and stall the EcoBoost (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: A part inside the fuel pump electronic control module can overheat and cut power to the fuel pump.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check for open recalls with your VIN. The dealer will inspect the module and replace it free if needed.

issues.t: Fuel delivery module can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell around the car or fuel dripping from under the rear seat area.
issues.why: The fuel delivery module on top of the tank can crack and leak fuel, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside and away from anything that could ignite it, and call a dealer. The module is replaced free under the recall.

issues.t: Halfshaft can slip out and cut drive to the wheels (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle suddenly loses drive while moving, as if it were in neutral, or rolls when parked without the parking brake.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the front halfshaft may not have been installed correctly, so the shaft can pull out of the linkshaft.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when parking until the recall is done. The dealer inspects the shaft and replaces parts free.

issues.t: Turbo oil supply line can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: A burning-oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or oil spots under the engine.
issues.why: Some turbocharger oil supply tubes were not brazed properly and can leak oil onto hot engine parts.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Stop and turn off the engine if you see smoke. Check for open recalls; the dealer will inspect and replace the tubes free.

issues.t: Rear toe link can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the vehicle pulling or wandering, or uneven rear tire wear. A broken link makes the rear end hard to control.
issues.why: On some vehicles the rear suspension toe links can crack and fracture over time.
issues.next: Have the rear suspension checked if you notice clunks or wandering, and check your VIN for open recalls; affected links are replaced free.

issues.t: Door pillar trim can fly off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The trim panel on the pillar between the front and rear doors looks loose or lifted, or you hear wind noise or a rattle there.
issues.why: The trim was not pressed on firmly enough at the factory, and foam pads on its back weakened the adhesive tape, so it can come loose and fall onto the road.
issues.next: Press loose trim back or remove it until it can be fixed. The dealer will reattach both front pillar trims with adhesive for free.

issues.t: Loose starter or alternator cables can arc (recall)
issues.sym: Flickering lights, warning lights, a no-start, or a burning electrical smell under the hood.
issues.why: The power cables at the starter and alternator may not have been tightened properly, which can cause electrical arcing and a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not ignore a burning smell. Check for open recalls; the dealer will inspect and secure the cables for free.

issues.t: Backup camera picture can go blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the camera image is blank, flickers or looks distorted.
issues.why: A fault in the rearview camera can make the image drop out intermittently.
issues.next: Back up using your mirrors and by looking over your shoulder. Check for open recalls; the dealer will replace the camera as needed free.

issues.t: Parking brake may not fully hold (recall)
issues.sym: The vehicle may creep or roll on a slope with the parking brake set if the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: On some MKTs built in May 2015 the parking brake may not fully engage.
issues.next: Always put the shifter in Park. Check for open recalls; the dealer tests the parking brake and replaces the control assembly if needed.

issues.t: Limousine and hearse vacuum pump relay can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning electrical smell, or brake assist warnings, on MKTs built as limousines or hearses.
issues.why: On livery and hearse versions, the relay for the extra brake vacuum pump can overheat because of an internal fault or contamination, which is a fire risk.
issues.next: If you own or operate a livery or hearse MKT, check its VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a new relay for free.

issues.t: EcoBoost shudders and loses power under hard acceleration
issues.sym: The engine shudders, knocks or loses power when you accelerate hard, such as merging onto a highway. Some owners also see heavy smoke for a few seconds after a start.
issues.why: Owner reports point to turbo boost problems on the twin-turbo engine. Dealers have diagnosed underboost, sensor and transmission solenoid faults, and some cases were hard to repeat in the shop.
issues.next: Note when it happens and ask the shop to check for stored codes, boost leaks and turbo condition. A worn turbo is a major repair, so get a clear diagnosis before replacing parts.

issues.t: Glass roof panel shatters on its own
issues.sym: A loud bang overhead, then the fixed glass roof panel is shattered, often while driving and with nothing hitting it.
issues.why: Owners report the large fixed glass roof breaking without any impact. The exact cause has not been confirmed.
issues.next: Pull over safely and cover the opening. Check whether your auto insurance glass coverage applies, and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Tires wear out early
issues.sym: Tires, often the inner edges, wear out long before their expected life, sometimes around 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners report fast and uneven tire wear on the 2010 model, which usually points to alignment settings or worn suspension parts on a heavy vehicle.
issues.next: Have the alignment checked and ask for a printout. Rotate tires on schedule and check tread depth on the inner edges.

issues.t: No heat from the passenger-side vents
issues.sym: The driver side blows warm air but the passenger side stays cold, or the temperature on one side will not change.
issues.why: In dual-zone climate systems this usually means a failed temperature blend door actuator, a small motor behind the dash that moves the air door.
issues.next: Have the climate system checked for codes and actuator movement. It is not a safety issue, but the actuator is often behind trim panels.

issues.t: Keyless entry and start work only some of the time
issues.sym: The key fob or push-button start sometimes does not respond, the vehicle may say no key is detected, or the doors will not unlock.
issues.why: Owners report intermittent key fob and keyless system faults, which can come from a weak fob, the fob itself, or the vehicle receiver.
issues.next: Try a new fob battery first and use the backup key slot or method in the owner manual. If it continues, have the dealer test the fob and receiver.

issues.t: Blower fan speed changes on its own
issues.sym: With automatic climate control on, the fan speeds up and slows down by itself or gets stuck on one speed.
issues.why: RepairPal lists frequent fan speed changes as a common MKT complaint on vehicles with automatic temperature control. A failing blower speed control module is a common cause.
issues.next: Try the manual fan settings to see if the problem follows. Have the blower control module and wiring checked if it keeps happening.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle latches erratically
issues.sym: The seat belt does not click in reliably, pops out, or the belt warning stays on even when buckled.
issues.why: Owners report the buckle latch mechanism wearing or sticking, so it does not lock or sense the tongue correctly.
issues.next: A belt that will not latch is a safety problem. Have the buckle inspected and replaced; do not drive with that seat occupied until it latches reliably.

issues.t: Door ajar warning stays on
issues.sym: The door ajar message or light stays on with all doors closed, interior lights may stay on and drain the battery, and the alarm may act up.
issues.why: The switch built into one of the door latches stops reporting that the door is closed.
issues.next: Open and firmly close each door, and spray the latches with lubricant. If the warning stays, the shop can find which latch reads open and replace it.
